old: The human excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra. The kidneys are bean-shaped and lie between the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae. Each kidney has an outer cortex and an inner medulla made of medullary pyramids, and it contains about one million nephrons. A nephron has a glomerulus and a renal tubule. The tubule runs from Bowman's capsule to the PCT, Henle's loop, the DCT and finally the collecting duct. Urine forms in three steps: glomerular filtration, tubular reabsorption and tubular secretion. Filtration occurs through glomerular endothelium, basement membrane and podocytes of Bowman's capsule, and almost all blood constituents except proteins pass. The PCT reabsorbs nearly all nutrients and 70 to 80% of electrolytes and water. The descending limb of Henle's loop is permeable to water, while the ascending limb is impermeable to water but transports electrolytes. The collecting duct reabsorbs much water to concentrate urine. A counter-current mechanism involving Henle's loop and the vasa recta concentrates urine. Micturition begins when stretch receptors in the bladder wall signal the CNS.
